OK. As far as I can tell the discovery packet we send is standards compliant, so without any more information I can't see that the problem is on this side.

I've been working a bit with upnp (I wrote http://viric.name/cgi-bin/filegive) and I had to improve the original upnp code to handle more routers. In the current situation of syncthing (0.8.11) it fails to dialog with miniupnpd services (what most openwrt routing boxes use), quite a broad use case.
This is the 'diff' that fixed miniupnpd support in my case, iirc: http://viric.name/cgi-bin/filegive/fdiff?v1=930f380e66bb577f&v2=55d85e2c63402b22&sbs=0

Ok! Forget what I said until now about the changes I did to upnp.go. I finally tried to fix syncthing upnp, and here is the fix:

```
diff --git a/upnp/upnp.go b/upnp/upnp.go
index 9de719a..9c85b23 100644
--- a/upnp/upnp.go
+++ b/upnp/upnp.go
@@ -60,14 +60,12 @@ func Discover() (*IGD, error) {
                return nil, err
        }

-       search := []byte(`
-M-SEARCH * HTTP/1.1
-Host: 239.255.255.250:1900
-St: urn:schemas-upnp-org:device:InternetGatewayDevice:1
-Man: "ssdp:discover"
-Mx: 3
-
-`)
+       search := []byte("M-SEARCH * HTTP/1.1\r\n" +
+"Host: 239.255.255.250:1900\r\n" +
+"St: urn:schemas-upnp-org:device:InternetGatewayDevice:1\r\n" +
+"Man: \"ssdp:discover\"\r\n" +
+"Mx: 3\r\n" +
+"\r\n")

        _, err = socket.WriteTo(search, ssdp)
        if err != nil {
```

@viric Thanks! I've incorporated the changes that seemed relevant (the spurious line break at the start, and the \r\n line endings. It still works for me against linux-igd, so I hope this works for miniupnpd as well.

Do a `tcpdump -n -i <name of network device> -s0 -A host <ip of gateway>` on the box running syncthing, before starting it. Should record a nice trace of the conversation between syncthing and the gateway, might give us some clues.

The less other stuff running at the same time, the better. Filter out anything obviously related to other activity you want to hide. :)

Do you know if upnp works for any other program in your computer?

You can install miniupnpc and check the result of:
upnpc -l
